tools.name: chipmunk_chiphorde
tools.note: lab moved autosome.ru -> autosome.org; the old page redirects to the github org and never names the new domain, so no rule here finds it

tools.name: PlantTFDB 2.0
tools.note: the old PKU page carries a Gao Lab migration notice; from_relocation now finds this independently

tools.name: Eponine
tools.note: Sanger moved to /tool/<name>/; HOST_REWRITES now finds this independently

tools.name: BroadPeak
tools.note: the tool's own page is gone (/page/software/ is a 404) and the old host redirects to the lab root, dropping the path. Curation decision: the lab that wrote it beats a dead link, even though the page never names BroadPeak

tools.name: ChIPnorm
tools.note: EPFL archived the lab and redirects every path to the archive root; re-appending software.html reaches the page. from_kept_path now does this

tools.name: MINDY
tools.note: the lab ships MINDY2 and CINDy as one entry, so Cindy.jar is MINDY2's download - the lab's own page links exactly this url, behind an Outlook safelink. The software index names and describes MINDY, unlike BroadPeak's lab root

tools.name: PAnDA (Protein And DNA Associations)
tools.note: the catalog's s.tartaglialab.com became service.tartaglialab.com. from_kept_path finds the submission form at tools.tartaglialab.com/new_submission/panda, which is the tool but a 1kB javascript shell that verifies only as undecided; this tutorial page describes PAnDA and names Tartaglia, so it verifies and tells a reader more

tools.name: EpiAnnotator
tools.note: NOT FOUND, and searched exhaustively: the paper calls it an R package with a web interface, but it is on neither CRAN, Bioconductor nor PyPI, absent from all 55 CompEpigen repos and from the Bock lab's, both authors have zero public repos, and computational-epigenomics.com now redirects to a DKFZ division page that never names it. Recorded so the search is not repeated
